rows: Fire Department reported flagpoles bending. According to the EF scale this would require winds near 70 MPH.
The tornado touched down just east of the intersection of Highways 548 and 276. Two barns were completely destroyed and fences were downed. Estimated wind speeds were 80 MPH.
Numerous trees and power lines downed.
A spotter estimated 60 mph winds in Rowlett.
Nickel size hail fell at the intersection of Highway 66 and Interstate 30 east of Rockwall.
Small limbs were reported down at the intersection of Highway 66 and Interstate 30 east of Rockwall.

A tornado caused mainly roof damage to several brick homes on the southeast side of Lake Ray Hubbard near Heath. Another home had its chimney knocked over and some large tree damage also occurred along the path of this tornado. The winds were estimated to be between 85-95 mph.
Golf ball to baseball sized hail was reported in Heath.
Half dollar sized hail fell at the Walmart located near Interstate 30 and Ridge Road in Rockwall.
Hail up to the size of tea cups fell in eastern Rockwall County. This large hail was falling from the tornadic supercell that also produced the EF-2 tornado south of Royse City.

Quarter sized hail was reported near State Highway 66 and FM 205 northeast of Rockwall.
A 62 MPH wind gust was reported on the east side of Heath.
A church that was being built on Erby Campbell Blvd in Royse City was knocked down by strong thunderstorm winds. Only the wood frame of the building was in place at the time.
Nickel to Quarter sized hail south of Fate, near the intersections of FM551 and State Highway 276.
Amateur Radio operators reported nickel sized hail near Union Valley.

Thunderstorm wind estimated near 60 mph caused minor damage to the roofs of 3 or 4 homes and 2 businesses near the Rockwall/Fate city border. The location of damage was just north of Interstate 30 and just east of FM 549.
Fire and rescue reported that about a dozen homes were damaged within the 100 Block of Jerome Prairie and 200 block of Cottonwood.
Emergency Management reported that a power line was blown down on Goliad Street between the First Baptist Church and Emma Jame.
Dime to quarter sized hail was observed in southeast Wylie.
One inch diameter hail was observed near downtown Rockwall.
The automated weather station at Rockwall Municipal Airport reported a 54 kt wind gust. In the area, damage to fences and carports was reported.

The Garland / Rowlett tornado continued across a small tract of land in western Rockwall County. The tornado continued doing significant damage in the City of Rowlett, before moving onto Lake Ray Hubbard and dissipating over the lake.

Amateur radio reported two-inch diameter hail in Royce City, TX.
Thunderstorm wind gust knocked down power lines across Interstate 30 and MM 76 in Royse City.
Several media outlets filmed the aftermath of significant damage to homes in the northern parts of Rockwall. In particular were homes in a subdivision east of John King Blvd and south of FM 552.
Storm spotter reported quarter size hail in Royse City.
Storm spotter reported half dollar size hail in Royse City.
Amateur radio reported golf ball sized hail in the city of Rockwall, TX.

A trained spotter reported ping-pong ball sized hail about 5 miles southeast of Fate, TX.
Wind damage was reported along Washington Street in Rockwall. Damage to athletic field fences, broken tree limbs, and wooden sheds were damaged.

A public report indicated ping pong ball sized hail about a mile south-southeast of Rockwall, TX.
